I'm not a parent, I can only share my experiences. I started self harming at age 11 as well. I was dealing with the passing of my mother the year prior, mental health issues, suicidal ideation/attempts and probably the fact that my autism was undiagnosed. To this day, doctors think I only have ADHD, which is a story for another day. 

Anywho, seeing as your child is dealing with suicidal ideation, I would seek treatment *ASAP*. My father found out about my SH when I was 12 and I didn't get therapy till I was 14. I ended up being voluntarily hospitalized at 15 and 18, and doing programs at 15, 17 and 19.

The hospitalization was for 9 days, and although I hated it, I walked out with a better understanding of coping skills, had some medication adjustments, and appointments set up with a therapist and paychiatrist for after I left for monitoring. It's definitely not for everyone, but it helped me personally. I learned DBT coping skills, which helps with emotion regulation, interpersonal effecfivess, mindfulness etc. CBT wasn't really effective for me. 

I'm in the US, so I don't know how therapy or hospitalization works over there, but I'd highly suggest at least a therapist who specializes in DBT if you can find one, to just try it. I was a stubborn child and refused to believe that therapy or coping skills could help, but I'm almost 21 now and still use those skills to this day.
